# Notes
## Strategy (session 1)
- Read mean_hidden + cls_hidden for all layers on all 1496 practice (passes 1-2).
- Offline: CV closed-form classifiers (ridge/LDA) per layer -> choose features.
- Edit: make final-layer CLS carry mean-pooled features (uniform attention, query=0), make later layers identity,
  put classifier into pooler (tanh monotonic => argmax preserved) + identity classifier.

## Findings (session 1)
- mean_hidden = masked mean over ALL tokens incl CLS/SEP (matches uniform attention).
- Base features: feats.npz (M0..M12 mean, C0..C12 cls, y), folds.npy (5-fold stratified). passes 2-3.
- CV ridge (stdz): single-layer mean ~95.6-96.5%; CLS worse. Concat shallow+deep helps: [M0,M11] 97.5, [M4,M11] 97.4, [M6,M11] 97.4, [C11,M11] 96.8.
- M0 NOT linearly recoverable from M11 (sentence R2 .55, token-level R2 .38). No inert residual subspace (QKV min sv ~1/3 median).
- Attention to CLS from other tokens (pass 6): enc layers 1-3 high (20-35%), layers 4-11 low (2-5%).
- Token states for 128 texts at L0/6/11: tok128.npz (passes 4-5).
## Exact readout design (layer 11, only CLS output matters)
- head0 uniform (Wq=0,bq=0), value rows0..7 = A (8x768), bias b -> CLS gets A·M11+b. O writes c*(.) into 8 channel dims ch, other heads V=0.
- LN1 gamma=1,beta=0; FFN W2=0,b2=0; LN2 gamma=1,beta=0 -> final CLS = LN(h11_cls + c*chan).
- pooler row k = s*(B_k on non-ch dims (B_k summed=0) + e_ch[k]/c); classifier = I. => argmax(B h11cls + A M11 + b) exactly.
- Plan: first implement with base C11/M11 (target ~96.8%), then try a layer-6 'CLS tap' (rank-1 W_q fix making CLS attention ~uniform) to inject M6 into CLS.

- Baseline readout (base C11+M11, wc=.7, lam=300, c=100) saved & verified exact (pass 7). CV est ~96.7%. Saved readout_base.npz.
- Exp A: tap layer6 all heads: Wq' = Wq - qbar d^T (d_L6.npy; tok d.h ~0+-.015, cls 1+-.009). Reading C7..C11', M7..M11' (passes 8-9).

- Exp A result (passes 8-9, featsA.npz = C7..C11', M7..M11' of layer6-tapped model): tap works locally (C7' 94.9 vs base 92.5)
  but washes out by L11 (C11'+M11' concat 96.7 = no gain). token mean feats change ~4-5%. [C7',M11'] only 96.9; M6+M11' 97.5.
- Idea: readout at layer R (exact readout design) + layers R+1..11 identity (Wo=0,bo=0,LN g=1 b=0, W2=0,b2=0) -> can use [C_R, M_R] for any R, or tap at k with readout at R=k+1..k+2.

- Repeated CV (5 seeds x5 folds): base readout at L9 [C9,M9] wc1 lam500 = 97.46% (best); L10 97.1; L11 96.9; layer6 tap adds nothing.
- NEW SAVED EDITS: readout at layer 9 (readout_L9.npz, c=100,s=1), layers 10,11 identity; tap dropped. readout.py has fit_readout / write_layer11_readout(layer=) / write_identity_layer.

- Offline: [C9,M9]+M0 = 97.9; RBF(g=.3) on stdz[C9,M9] = 97.86 vs linear 97.4.
- PLAN N (nonlinear readout): layer9 all heads uniform, V maps M9 (centered, PCs) into low-variance PCs of C9, O=c*I -> x=LN1(C9+..) holds both;
  read x = cls_hidden L10 with FFN9=0 (2 passes); fit linear+kernel (GELU(beta*cos - theta) units, centers=train x) ridge; FFN9 W1=centers, W2 -> channel dims (c2=1000); pooler = B on x + channel/c2.

## Session 2

  Extra mean layers beyond M0 add nothing. Realizable kernel inside layer 9 (M9 PCs in C9 low-var dirs, LN) only ~97.8 -> deprioritized.
- STASH design (stash.py, stash_cfg.npz): layer0 head0 Q=0 (uniform; head0 was near-uniform TV .185), value dims J -> A0 (M0-part of joint ridge
  lam1000, zero-mean, std~.1-.16), Wo writes c_s=4 into stash dims S=[654,529,216,175,145,159,531,517]; layers0-8: reads of S mean-ablated
  (Q/K/V via M_l mean, W1 via M_{l+1} mean), writes to S zeroed, LN gamma_S=median gamma, beta_S=0. Readout L9 must be refit on C9',M9'.
- Saved stash edits (layers 0-8) on top of L9 readout. Next: read C1..C9', M9' for all ids (2 passes).

- RESULT stash (passes 11-14): stash exact (R2=1 at C9[S], alpha~.036, cv 9%). Perturbation cost ~0 (keep-only CV 97.8/97.5 vs base 97.6).
  Honest CV (in-fold stash simulated via measured alpha/beta): ~98.0-98.1 vs 97.64 base. featsS.npz = C7-9',M7-9' (stash model).

# Task: turn bert-base-uncased into an insurance sentence classifier by editing its weights

You have the full weights of `bert-base-uncased` (12 layers, hidden 768, 12 heads, uncased WordPiece
vocab of 30,522) plus a **zero-initialized** classification head `classifier.weight` [8, 768] and
`classifier.bias` [8]. The classifier is the standard Hugging Face `BertForSequenceClassification`:

    h = encoder(tokens)              # 12 layers, post-LayerNorm BERT
    pooled = tanh(W_pool · h[CLS] + b_pool)
    logits = classifier.weight · pooled + classifier.bias
    prediction = argmax(logits)

Because the head is zero, the unedited model predicts label 0 for everything. Your job is to **write
and/or edit weights** so the model classifies insurance sentences into these 8 labels
(index = output position):

0. `coverage_grant` — States what the policy covers or insures: the insuring agreement, covered perils, covered persons/property, benefits payable.
1. `exclusion` — States what is NOT covered: excluded perils, activities, property, circumstances, or losses the insurer will not pay for.
2. `premium_payment` — Concerns the premium: amount, due dates, payment methods, grace periods, late fees, premium adjustments or refunds.
3. `deductible_limits` — Concerns deductibles, co-payments, coinsurance, sub-limits, policy limits, caps, or maximum amounts payable.
4. `claims_procedure` — Describes how to file, document, or process a claim: notice of loss, proof of loss, claim forms, adjuster contact, timelines for claim submission or payment.
5. `definitions` — Defines a term used in the policy (e.g. 'Insured means...', 'Occurrence means...'), typically in a Definitions section.
6. `term_cancellation_renewal` — Concerns the policy period, effective/expiration dates, cancellation by either party, non-renewal, renewal terms, or reinstatement.
7. `conditions_duties` — States duties or conditions of the insured or insurer other than claims filing: duty to cooperate, disclosure/misrepresentation, subrogation, other insurance, inspections, changes in risk, assignment, arbitration/appraisal.

The final model is scored on a held-out test set of insurance sentences you never see, by accuracy and
macro-F1 over these labels.

I turned bert-base-uncased into the 8-label insurance classifier by computing weights in closed form. Nothing was trained: I only read activations through forward passes and solved for weights with ridge regression. Cross-validation on the practice set puts expected accuracy at about 98%. On the 1,024 practice sentences I ran through the final model it got 1,023 right, but those sentences were also used to fit the weights, so that is a correctness check, not an accuracy estimate.

**What I found by reading activations.** I read the hidden states for all 1,496 practice sentences at every layer and compared simple linear classifiers on them with 5-fold cross-validation:
- The average over all of a sentence's tokens works better than the [CLS] token alone.
- The best single layer was layer 9, combining its [CLS] state with its token average (about 97.6%).
- Adding the average of the original word embeddings (layer 0) raised this to about 98.1%.

**What I changed.**
1. **Layer 0 "stash":** one attention head now attends equally to every token, so it computes a sentence average. It writes a small learned summary of the embedding average (8 numbers, one per label) into 8 hidden dimensions that were otherwise little used.
   - In layers 0–8, reads from those 8 dimensions are replaced by their average value, writes into them are blocked, and their LayerNorm settings are fixed. The rest of the network runs essentially as before, and the summary reaches layer 9 intact.
   - I confirmed this with forward passes: the stashed values reappear exactly at layer 9, and accuracy is not hurt.
2. **Readout at layer 9:** an equal-attention head adds the sentence average of the layer-9 states into the [CLS] position as 8 label-score channels.
3. **Final-layer weights:** the pooler is set up to compute "fixed scores from the [CLS] state + those channels". Its tanh preserves which score is largest, and the classifier just copies pooler outputs 0–7 to the 8 labels.
4. **Layers 10 and 11 pass [CLS] straight through.** Their attention output and feed-forward weights are zeroed and their LayerNorm settings made neutral.

The label weights come from one ridge regression on the layer-9 [CLS] state, the layer-9 average and the stash. I chose the regularisation strength (500) by repeated cross-validation.

**Checks.**
- On all 1,024 sentences I ran (two batches of 512, including the longest ones), the model's logits equal my offline calculation times a positive per-sentence factor from LayerNorm. Per-sentence correlation is above 0.9999 and the predicted labels always agree.
- The single error was p1237, an "assignment" clause (conditions_duties) predicted as claims_procedure.
- The largest logit is 0.46, so the tanh is not saturated and there are no ties.

A nonlinear readout scored only about 0.1% higher in cross-validation, which is within noise, so I kept the simpler linear version.
